text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as crude oil prices hit five-month highs, with U.S. oil climbing above $101 per barrel and Brent crude reaching $126.55 amid escalating Middle East tensions. Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and oil facilities this week, and Iran signaled it has prepared military responses to potential U.S. strikes—both developments pushing investors to bid up oil prices and the energy stocks that benefit from them.

The stock's 12.6% gain over two weeks tracks closely with the sharp rally in crude itself, driven by real geopolitical risk rather than company-specific news. As long as Middle East tensions remain elevated and oil supplies face potential disruption, refiners and major producers like this one tend to see their valuations supported.
